# CWN Free Edition parity matrix (#1025, milestone 1)

**Generated by `tools/cwn_fe_parity.py`; do not edit by hand.**

Table of contents captured from the CWN Free Edition PDF (081123, 231 pages) at
`data/rules/cwn_fe_toc.json`. The SRD at <https://cwn.quadrifons.com/> is a cross-check only: it omits
optional sections and the Antagonists & NPCs material, so several Free Edition sections below have no
SRD counterpart.

Every section of the Free Edition's own table of contents, in book order, mapped to the module that
implemented it and the test that exercises it.

| Status | Means |
|---|---|
| `tested` | a module implements it **and** a test references it. Evidence of implementation, **not** proof that every subprocedure on those pages is covered — that is the per-procedure audit. |
| `untested` | a module exists but no test references it. |
| `missing` | nothing implements it. |
| `setting` | the book's section is prose or advice rather than a procedure, with the reason given. |

Silence is never read as done.

| Status | Sections |
|---|---:|
| tested | 43 |
| untested | 0 |
| missing | 30 |
| setting | 25 |
| **total** | **98** |

## Reading the gaps

The rules half (character creation through hacking) is largely implemented and tested. The **GM half is
not**: dystopia and city generation, megacorp and gang generators, NPC creation and stat blocks, schemes,
mission tags and types, intrusion missions, rewards, **Heat**, reaction rolls, morale, and the NPC
roster chapters have no implementing module at all. Cyberware, cyberdecks, pharmaceuticals, demons and
watchdogs, and network architecture are likewise missing on the Python side.

Those are the actual backlog. This matrix does not claim otherwise, and no section is marked `tested`
on the strength of a data file or a filename.
